latest_apis.rationale: Every Qwik/Qwik City API in use is the current documented one on the latest stable (1.20.3), with zero deprecated-era patterns. The one notable gap is that nearly all internal links use plain <a> rather than <Link>, which per qwik.dev/docs/routing/ forfeits SPA navigation and prefetch — a missed current API rather than a legacy one, so 4 not 5.

No filler packages; exact pinning aids reproducible harness builds. Nitpick: qwik sits in dependencies where the starter puts it in devDependencies, which is harmless here.

churn_resistance.rationale: Data access is properly behind one module and the scaffold is the canonical current one, so a Qwik upgrade would touch few files. But the API boundary is untyped (Promise<any> plus pervasive any-casts), a spec constant is duplicated, and build artifacts are left unignored — enough loose edges that a requirement or data change ripples more than it should.

findings.issue: Internal navigation uses raw <a href> (also moves-table.tsx:116-119, pokemon-cards.tsx:24, routes/types/index.tsx:18, routes/types/[name]/index.tsx:96,118, routes/moves/[name]/index.tsx:66, routes/pokemon/[name]/index.tsx:183,264) instead of qwik-city's <Link>, which layout.tsx and not-found.tsx do use. Per qwik.dev/docs/routing/, plain <a> performs a full navigation and downgrades the app out of SPA context, losing prefetch and scroll restoration on the app's primary browse loop.
findings.suggestion: Use <Link> from '@builder.io/qwik-city' for all internal URLs (optionally with a small href helper in lib/api.ts), so prefetch/SPA navigation and scroll restoration work uniformly.

findings.issue: apiGet is typed Promise<any> and every downstream consumer casts with any, so the PokeAPI boundary — the thing the spec says is a live service whose data changes — has no compile-time protection.
findings.suggestion: Declare interfaces for the API response shapes used (NamedAPIResource, Pokemon, Species, Move, Ability, Type, Generation) in lib/api.ts and type apiGet<T>; loaders then keep their typed CardData/MoveRow view models.

findings.issue: Build output (44 hashed bundles in dist/build, server/entry.node-server.js, q-manifest.json, 404.html, sitemap.xml) is present in the working tree and no .gitignore covers app/ (root .gitignore only has /data/, /.data-cache/, node_modules/), so stale artifacts can get committed and drift from sources.
findings.suggestion: Add app/.gitignore with dist/, server/, tmp/ (the standard qwik starter ignores exactly these).

findings.issue: Outbound fetches have no timeout or AbortSignal, so a slow or hung upstream stalls the route loader and the SSR response indefinitely.
findings.suggestion: Use AbortSignal.timeout(n) around the fetch (and cache the rejection, which it already does) to fail fast on a dead API.

findings.issue: idFromUrl extracts ids with a regex from resource URLs instead of using the platform's URL parser.
findings.suggestion: Number(new URL(url).pathname.split('/').filter(Boolean).pop()) — or at minimum keep the regex but this is exactly the case the URL API exists for.

findings.issue: EXCLUDED_TYPES duplicates the identical set declared in lib/api.ts:50; adding a new excluded type (the data already has stellar/shadow/unknown and the spec is explicit about the rule) requires two coordinated edits.
findings.suggestion: Export EXCLUDED_TYPES from lib/api.ts and import it here.

findings.issue: target ES2020 / lib ES2022 on an app that runs only on Node 24 and the latest Chromium; the emitted JS is downleveled for engines that will never run it.
findings.suggestion: Bump target to ES2022+ (the current qwik starter trend is ESNext for the browser target); runtime behavior is unchanged for this codebase.

findings.issue: @builder.io/qwik and @builder.io/qwik-city are in dependencies; the current create-qwik scaffold puts them in devDependencies since the build bundles everything (server/entry.node-server.js has no runtime import of them).
findings.suggestion: Move both to devDependencies — harmless either way, but matching the scaffold avoids surprises when Qwik 2's migration guide ('Move qwik packages to devDependencies') lands.

summary: This is a well-aimed, current-generation Qwik City app: it pins the actual latest stable (1.20.3), uses only documented-current APIs (routeLoader$ with status()/resolveValue, useSignal/useNavigate, nodeServerAdapter), and carries a lean five-dependency manifest with vite deliberately kept inside Qwik 1.x's supported range. The main forward-looking weakness is that nearly every internal link is a plain <a> rather than <Link>, throwing away the framework's SPA/prefetch navigation on the app's core browse loop. Boundary typing (Promise<any>) and unignored build output are the remaining churn risks.
